headline: Record shipments and the border-wall contract lift Reliance
summary_short: Reliance's Q2 2026 net sales rose 26.5% y/y to $4.63 billion on record tons sold and higher selling prices, with diluted EPS up 42.3% to $6.29 as the U.S. border wall contract contributed $0.41 per share.
summary_long: Net sales grew 26.5% y/y to $4.63 billion as tons sold rose 10.8% (including a 5.2-point contribution from the U.S. border wall contract) and average selling price improved 14.5%. LIFO gross margin fell to 28.1% from 29.7% on higher carbon-steel and aluminum product costs, though FIFO margin was roughly flat. SG&A grew with volume-related warehousing/delivery costs and incentive comp, but per-ton SG&A rose only 0.9% as the border wall contract's lower-cost profile aided leverage. Net income rose 38.2% to $322.9 million and diluted EPS rose 42.3% to $6.29. The board declared a $1.25 per-share Q3 dividend; the company repurchased no shares in Q2. No numeric forward guidance was given in the filing.

drivers.explanation: Record tons sold (+10.8% y/y, including a 5.2pp contribution from the U.S. border wall contract) plus a 14.5% higher average selling price drove net sales growth.
LIFO gross margin fell to 28.1% from 29.7% as higher carbon-steel and aluminum costs raised LIFO expense; FIFO margin, which excludes LIFO, was roughly flat y/y.
Higher selling prices and improved operating leverage, aided by the border wall contract's below-average SG&A-per-ton profile, lifted operating income margin.
